explanations.explanation: Yes, friend, a mustard seed. Jesus says the kingdom of God "…is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden." (Luke 13:19) Of all the seeds He could have picked, He picked that one. I'd have said chocolate chip, but that's why He's teaching and I'm stamping.

Wheat is a solid guess, friend, because people plant it all the time. But Jesus doesn't go to the wheat field here. He says the kingdom of God "…is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden." (Luke 13:19) Mustard, the tiny one. Wheat is sitting in the parking lot wondering why nobody called.

Barley is a good guess for a seed, friend, but it isn't the one Jesus picks here. He says the kingdom of God "…is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden." (Luke 13:19) Mustard is the seed this time. Barley has to wait for another passage.
True, friend! Jesus says of the seed, "It grew and became a tree…" (Luke 13:19) One tossed seed, and it turns into a tree. I once tossed a single raisin into dough and all I got was a lumpy cookie.
It's actually true, friend. Jesus says the mustard seed "…grew and became a tree…" (Luke 13:19) The seed doesn't stay a seed. I'll admit I nearly tripped on this one myself, so no shame here.
Yes, friend, the birds of the air! Jesus says they "…nested in its branches." (Luke 13:19) The seed grows into a tree, and the tree gets tenants. That's a whole neighborhood from one tossed seed.

Beasts of the field is a fun guess, friend. But Jesus doesn't list them here. He says "…the birds of the air nested in its branches." (Luke 13:19) Nesting up in branches is bird business. I bet a beast trying to climb up there would make a lot of noise on the way.

Locusts in the tree? Friend, that would be a rough ending for any garden. Jesus says it's "…the birds of the air…" that "…nested in its branches." (Luke 13:19) Birds are the ones moving in, not locusts.

Leaven, friend! Jesus says, "It is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour…" (Luke 13:21) That's the second picture. Leaven is what makes dough rise, and I know a thing or two about dough.

Salt is a good kitchen word, friend, and I'd never turn it down. But Jesus doesn't use it here. He says the kingdom of God "…is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour…" (Luke 13:21) The word to fill in is leaven.

Oil, friend? I can see you reaching for something from the pantry. But Jesus says the kingdom of God "…is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour…" (Luke 13:21) Leaven is the picture here, and oil isn't in the passage.
All, friend! The woman mixes the leaven in "…until all of it was leavened." (Luke 13:21) Not a corner left out, not one pocket of flour skipped. Every bit of it gets reached.
Half is a sensible guess, friend, but the text goes further. The woman mixes the leaven in "…until all of it was leavened." (Luke 13:21) She doesn't stop partway. The word is all.

Most is close, friend, and I respect a near miss. But Jesus says the woman mixed the leaven in "…until all of it was leavened." (Luke 13:21) Not most of it. All of it. That's the word that fits the blank.
